blocks.h2: How a Tankless Water Heater Works
blocks.body: A tankless heater warms water only when a tap is open. Water passes through a heat exchanger, a burner or element heats it instantly and it flows to the fixture. Nothing is stored, so there's no tank for sediment to settle in and no standby heat loss. In hard water, though, minerals can build up inside the heat exchanger, so regular descaling is part of owning one.

items.q: Can a tankless heater handle McHenry's hard water?
items.preview: Yes, with regular descaling and ideally a softener.
items.answer: Yes. Hard water builds scale in the heat exchanger, so it needs regular descaling. A softener ahead of it reduces how often. We set up every install with valves that make descaling simple.

items.q: How often should I descale my tankless water heater?
items.preview: Often once a year in hard water.
items.answer: In hard water, often about once a year, sometimes more with heavy use. Your unit may show a scale warning when it's due.

items.q: Why does my tankless heater shut off mid-shower?
items.preview: Often scale, a dirty filter or a flow issue.
items.answer: Scale in the heat exchanger, a clogged inlet filter or a flow problem can all cause shutdowns. A service visit with descaling usually fixes it.

items.q: Will I need a bigger gas line?
items.preview: Sometimes. We check before we quote.
items.answer: Sometimes. Tankless units draw a lot of gas when they fire. We check your line and include any upgrade in the price.
